symptom: `create user role Administrator (…)` — the role a blank app ships — passes `check --references` ('Check passed!') and exec then refuses it ('user role already exists') after the statements before it were written. Same for a plain create of an existing menu, queue, scheduled event, regular expression, message definition collection, database connection, REST client, OData client/service, configuration
cause: These create statements were in neither stmtCreateKind nor projectNameSets.setFor. TestEveryCreateDocTypeIsProjectChecked compared those two switches with each other, so a type missing from BOTH was invisible to it — the guard had no independent source of 'every create'
file: mdl/executor/validate_duplicates.go (stmtCreateKind, stmtDropInfo, setFor, loadProjectNameSets, listedQualifiedNames, projectSetHas/execFoldsExistingName), validate_duplicates_coverage_test.go (TestEveryCreateStmtIsClassified)
fix: Classify the kinds, give them drops and project sets (generic reflection over Backend.List*, fold-aware where the handler folds). New guard scans mdl/ast source for every Create* type with an isStatement method and requires stmtCreateKind to name it or createStmtsNotClassified to record why (validation rule, translations, external entities; annotation recorded as a KNOWN GAP)
insight: A guard that compares two hand-maintained lists only catches drift between them; it needs a third, independent source — here the AST package's own declarations — or a type absent from both lists passes forever. Running the new guard against the old code surfaced 15 such create statements, not just the one reported — 11 of them refused by exec and now checked, 4 recorded with a reason
